subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 2-hour-old boy delivered at 36 weeks' gestation has a temperature of 35.4 C and is otherwise well. He is placed under a radiant warmer, and his brown adipose tissue generates heat through nonshivering thermogenesis.
question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism of heat production by brown adipose tissue?

options.text: Increased ATP synthase activity in mitochondria
Increased expression of complex II in brown adipocytes
Inhibition of the electron transport chain at complex I
Uncoupling protein 1 increases inner mitochondrial membrane permeability to protons

explanation_correct: Uncoupling protein 1 (thermogenin) in brown fat increases the permeability of the inner mitochondrial membrane to protons, allowing them to re-enter the matrix without passing through ATP synthase. The energy of the proton gradient is released as heat, and electron transport continues while ATP synthesis decreases.

explanation_incorrect.A: Increased ATP synthase activity would increase ATP production, not heat production.
explanation_incorrect.B: Creatine phosphate hydrolysis buffers ATP in muscle and does not mediate nonshivering thermogenesis.
explanation_incorrect.C: Complex II is not the mediator of brown fat thermogenesis; uncoupling protein 1 is.
explanation_incorrect.D: Complex I inhibition would slow electron transport and reduce heat production.

educationalObjective: Uncoupling protein 1 (thermogenin) dissipates the proton gradient in brown adipose tissue to generate heat for nonshivering thermogenesis.
